title: Stagewise Kernel Heatmap Mapper for Prefill/Decode Scheduling
creator: Aisha Khan
description: Goal: Implement a light-weight stagewise "heatmap mapper" that ingests microkernel latency profiles across architecture variants and per-stage sequence-length distributions (prefill vs decode) to pick the best kernel variant at each execution stage. Motivation: current single-policy kernel pick (global seqlen median) misses stage-specific optima during long-context prefill or bursty decode patterns, causing suboptimal throughput and cost. Approach: 1) Collect short-run microbenchmarks (1-2k samples) for candidate microkernels on each arch (A100/H100/GPU-pool prototypes) across token lengths {32,64,128,256,512}. 2) Build a compressed stage heatmap: rows=kernel variants, cols=seqlen buckets, values=median token-ms. 3) At request time, compute expected seqlen mix for prefill and decode from sampling cache and route the prefill stage to the kernel minimizing expected token-ms subject to a latency budget; decodes use a different heatmap slice prioritizing single-token latency. 4) Fallback: if profiler lacks data for an arch/seqlen, use nearest-neighbor interpolation and conservative gating. Acceptance criteria: - End-to-end hosted API 99th percentile latency for chat workloads reduced by >=8% vs baseline for mixed prefill/decode traces. - Token-cost per 1M tokens reduced by >=6% on average across test corpus. - No regressions (>3%) on short-context inference (<=64 tokens). - Automated profiler runs integrated into nightly perf pipeline and displayed in Console perf dashboard. Implementation notes: keep runtime decision path lock-free and avoid memory-copying kernels during hotpath selection. Persist profiler artifacts keyed by model fingerprint+arch. Metrics: prefill p95, decode p99, cost-per-token, fallback-rate, profiler-staleness. Risks/trade-offs: extra perf down-samples for profiling can add noise; overly aggressive stage splits may increase cache misses. Mitigations: sampling window and exponential backoff for profiler refresh; conservative thresholding for switching kernels mid-session.
comments: 2026-02-26 — Kickoff: scoped two-week spike for heatmap data model and microbench harness. Spike owners: Luca + Mei. (Notes: drive/confluence link attached).

2026-03-02 — Spike results: initial heatmaps show H100 prefers kernel-v3 for seqlen>256 while A100 prefers kernel-v2; decode single-token latency sometimes favors microkernel-fused paths. Observed cost win ~9% in synthetic chat mix. Added conservative gating to avoid oscillation.

2026-03-05 — Architecture review with runtime team: agreed on per-model fingerprint keying and TTL=24h for profiler artifacts. Decision: keep selection logic in C++ hotpath with a tiny lookup table populated from Python orchestrator at startup. Action: ENG-108620 to implement C++ selector shim.

2026-03-09 — PR opened: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1428 — implements heatmap serializer and server-side loader. Requesting review from @samr and @nina. Perf baseline tests in CI failed for an edge case: memory-alignment on NVL kernel variants; fixed in subsequent commit.

2026-03-12 — Integration test: nightlies show p95 prefill down 11% on large-context chat profile; decode p99 down 4% (still within target). Noted a 1.8% regression on a specific short-LLM ensemble; added exclusion rule for that model in heatmap scope.
Next steps: roll canary to 10% of hosted traffic (dedicated tenant cluster) and monitor fallback-rate and cost metrics for 72h. Prepare runbook for rollback if error spike >2x baseline.
